limited-availability.statement: The Zscaler-managed Business Continuity Cloud is a limited-availability feature; tenants subscribe to it through their Zscaler Sales Representative.

quotes: This feature is in limited availability.
To subscribe to the Business Continuity Cloud service, contact your Zscaler Sales Representative.

uses-pse-data-plane.statement: The Business Continuity Cloud has a private data plane that leverages Private Service Edges for Internet and SaaS (and for Private Access) and a private control plane that includes the Private Policy Cache and Private PAC Server. The Private Policy Cache is integrated into the Private Service Edge infrastructure and applies the last known good policy to traffic.

quotes: The private data plane leverages the functionalities of Private Service Edges for Internet & SaaS and Private Service Edges for Private Access.
The private control plane leverages the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) components, such as Private Policy Cache and Private PAC Server
It is integrated into the existing Private Service Edges to apply the last known good policies to the traffic flow during failover to the private cloud.
This component is integrated into the Private Service Edge infrastructure and acts as a local repository for policy configurations

trigger-is-critical-failure.statement: The service mainly helps organizations stay connected and protected during critical failure scenarios in which the public clouds are unreachable.

quotes: The Business Continuity Cloud service mainly helps organizations stay connected and protected during critical failure scenarios, where public clouds are unreachable.

prerequisites.statement: Prerequisites for Internet and SaaS business continuity include Zscaler Client Connector 4.6 or later for Windows, Zscaler disaster recovery enabled in Client Connector, all security policies configured before entering business continuity, and GRE tunnel locations configured with authentication disabled.

quotes: The end users' machines are running Zscaler Client Connector versions 4.6 and later for Windows.
Zscaler disaster recovery is enabled in Zscaler Client Connector for end users.
All security policies are configured before entering business continuity.
The GRE tunnel locations are configured with authentication disabled to support business continuity.

z-tunnel-2-unsupported.statement: Zscaler Tunnel 2.0 is not supported in business continuity mode.

quotes: Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 is not supported in business continuity mode.

last-known-good-policy.statement: Only the last known good policy configuration applies to outgoing traffic in business continuity mode: recent policy updates might not take effect immediately, and new user authentication or enrollment is not supported.

quotes: Only the last known good policy configurations apply to outgoing traffic in business continuity mode.
Any recent organizational policy updates might not take immediate effect.
New user authentication or new user enrollment is not supported in business continuity mode.

redundant-pairs.statement: Private Policy Cache and Private PAC Servers are deployed in redundant pairs in each Business Continuity Cloud site; they are managed by Zscaler and subject to ongoing updates and enhancements at any time.

quotes: Both Private Policy Cache and Private PAC Servers are deployed in redundant pairs in each Business Continuity Cloud site.
They are managed by Zscaler and are subject to ongoing updates and enhancements at any time.

upgrade-delay.statement: During public cloud software upgrades the Business Continuity Cloud upgrade is delayed on purpose to prevent upgrade-related issues; this also delays the update of new policies or configurations, for fault isolation.

quotes: During public cloud software upgrades, the Business Continuity Cloud upgrade is delayed on purpose to prevent upgrade-related issues.
This also delays the update of any new policies or configurations to support fault isolation.

policy-cache-roles.statement: During normal operations the Private Policy Cache fetches, stores and regularly syncs tenant-specific configurations from the cloud so they are available in business continuity mode, and serves as the primary control path for local Service Edge instances; during business continuity it operates independently of public clouds to maintain security policies.

quotes: Fetches and stores tenant-specific configurations from the cloud and syncs them regularly to be readily available in business continuity mode.
Serves as the primary control path for local Service Edge instances, ensuring up-to-date policy availability for business continuity.
Operates independently of public clouds to maintain security policies.

pac-servers.statement: Private PAC Servers receive and locally store PAC files from the public cloud for each Business Continuity Cloud site; during business continuity they host disaster recovery PAC files that redirect client requests to the appropriate Business Continuity Cloud, and their geo-awareness lets Zscaler Client Connector connect to the nearest Business Continuity Cloud based on its IP address or location.

quotes: Receives and locally stores PAC files from the public cloud for each Business Continuity Cloud site.
Hosts disaster recovery PAC files to redirect client requests to the appropriate Business Continuity Cloud.
Provides geo-awareness, allowing Zscaler Client Connector to connect to the nearest Business Continuity Cloud based on its IP address or location.

bc-trigger-pse-outage.title: Whether a PSE or ZIA service outage triggers business continuity mode
bc-trigger-pse-outage.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'When the Business Continuity Cloud activates (during a PSE or ZIA service outage) ... PSE outages are one of the triggers.' The captured pages describe critical failure in which the public clouds are unreachable as the main case, and list blackouts, brownouts and critical failure as failure scenarios, but do not say that a customer's own Private Service Edge outage activates business continuity mode, or what activates it.

z-tunnel-2-fallback.title: What a Z-Tunnel 2.0 client does when business continuity mode starts
z-tunnel-2-fallback.detail: Unverified legacy statement (references/shared/cross-product-integrations.md): "Z-Tunnel 2.0 doesn't work in BC mode. Tenants migrated to 2.0 fall back to 1.0 during BC failover." The help says only that Z-Tunnel 2.0 is not supported in business continuity mode (claim z-tunnel-2-unsupported); it does not say whether clients fall back to Z-Tunnel 1.0 or lose service.
z-tunnel-2-fallback.blocks: planning business continuity for a Z-Tunnel 2.0 fleet

supported-connectivity-methods.summary: Whether IPSec tunnels are supported in business continuity mode.

quotes: The Internet & SaaS Business Continuity Cloud supports Zscaler Client Connector Z-Tunnel 1.0, PAC files, IPSec tunnel, and GRE tunnel connectivity.

positions.says: Z-Tunnel 1.0, PAC files, IPSec tunnel and GRE tunnel connectivity are supported.

quotes: The Internet & SaaS Business Continuity Cloud only supports Z-Tunnel 1.0, PAC files, and GRE tunnel connectivity.

positions.says: Only Z-Tunnel 1.0, PAC files and GRE tunnels are supported; IPSec is not listed.

supported-connectivity-methods.impact: A tenant that forwards to the Business Continuity Cloud over IPSec cannot rely on either page alone. Both pages agree that Z-Tunnel 2.0 is not supported and that GRE, PAC and Z-Tunnel 1.0 are.
